Noise versus evidence in triage conversations

Results for Claude Haiku. Complete run: 11,718 conversations (3 reversal cases and 10 vignettes, 3 repeats each), 128,898 replies, Claude Haiku. 2,588 replies (2.0%) carry a one-off diagnosis wording that was not read and are left out of the diagnosis figures.

11,718 conversations and 128,898 replies are in these figures:

  • core10: 8,964 conversations, 10 vignettes, 3 repeat(s)
  • reversal: 2,754 conversations, 3 vignettes, 3 repeat(s)

How to read these. Urgency figures use the direction of change (more urgent, unchanged, less urgent), which does not depend on the clinicians' reference level. Diagnosis figures use the replies whose diagnosis has been read (2,588 of 128,898 replies have not been read and are left out). Diagnoses were judged by their leading part, with a rule checked against full readings on 150 strings; no clinician has reviewed the readings.

Timing and persistence

Is the effect of timing more than chance?

Two tests, two questions. The first p-value asks whether timing matters in these conversations: the timings are shuffled 2,000 times within each vignette, language, speaker and noise type, and the linear trend is compared with the shuffled ones. The second asks whether the effect would carry over to new vignettes: each vignette gives one number (uptake after reply 10 minus uptake after reply 1) and a t-test asks whether their mean differs from zero. No correction for multiple tests has been applied.

Shares are the mean of the per-vignette shares. No correction for multiple tests has been applied; with this many rows, treat p-values near 0.05 as weak.

Vignette by vignette

Stated confidence and agreement between repeats

The first reply is the cleanest test, because every conversation of one vignette, language and speaker starts from the identical message (102 replies per starting message). There, replies stating a confidence below 70 gave the commonest urgency level 81% of the time (n = 2,178); replies stating 80 or more gave it 97% of the time (n = 1,378). Stated urgency confidence sits in a narrow band: half of all first replies state between 70 and 75.
